Bug_Details:
Reported as "Arbitrary Code Execution Under lock" by starvation.

A call that may execute arbitrary code (such as registered, or chained, callbacks) is made while holding a lock.
This code may deadlock whenever the callbacks obtain locks themselves, so it is an unsafe pattern.

Example:

SettableFuture future = null;  public void callFutureSet() {    future.set(null);  }  // synchronized means it's taking a lock implicitly  public synchronized void example_of_bad_pattern() {    callFutureSet(); // <- issue reported here  }  // If the call is made while holding multiple locks, the warning  // will be issued only at the innermost lock acquisition. Here we  // report in example_of_bad_pattern but we won't report below.  public void nested_bad_pattern_no_report(Object o) {    synchronized (o) {      example_of_bad_pattern(); // <- no issue reported    }  }
Bug_Explanation: The bug is embedded in the generated code by having a method `example_of_bad_pattern` that is synchronized (thus holding a lock) and calls another method `callFutureSet` which may execute arbitrary code (simulated by setting a value in `SettableFuture`). This pattern can lead to deadlock if the callbacks in `callFutureSet` obtain locks themselves.
Trigger_Explanation: The test calls the showBug method, which internally calls example_of_bad_pattern. This method is synchronized and calls callFutureSet, which simulates setting a value in SettableFuture and potentially executing callbacks. This pattern can lead to deadlock if the callbacks in callFutureSet obtain locks themselves.
